title: AI Winters: Boom and Bust
tagline: Date ten AI claims, separate forecasts from assessments, and compare two contractions without forcing a cycle
hub_blurb: Classify and date ten sourced claims, then compare two AI winters through evidence rather than a prediction script.
card_blurb: A curated selection of ten sourced claims: five time-bounded forecasts to score; four dated assessments or untimed ambitions to classify without grading against the future; and one warning that was testable and correct. A scrubbable timeline then compares claims, institutional bets, constraints, reassessment, and withdrawal across two historically different contractions.
description: **AI Winters: Boom and Bust** — a phone-first, single-file, offline inquiry into two twentieth-century AI contractions and the limits of historical analogy. Act I distinguishes forecasts, which need an outcome and deadline, from contemporary assessments, which need evidence about their own time. It is a curated teaching selection, not a representative accuracy sample. Act II uses five comparison lenses across a sourced 1950–2026 timeline; it does not claim a fixed causal sequence. Act III contrasts the first winter, the second winter, and current conditions while keeping unestablished constraints and any withdrawal openly unresolved. Act IV weighs similarities and differences, including source-bounded present-day evidence. Every claim resolves to a retrievable source and is marked primary or reported; a live self-test demonstrates source coverage; and a public cut list records excluded claims.
